items.stem: What is the main job of HTML on a web page?

options.text: It gives the page its structure and content, like headings, text and images
options.rationale: Correct: HTML provides structure and content; CSS handles appearance.
HTML structures content; it does not change computer speed.
HTML is for structure, not password storage.
Colours are mainly CSS; HTML is structure.

items.explanation: Correct: HTML provides structure and content; CSS handles appearance.

items.stem: Which TWO are good accessibility practices for a web page? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Adding meaningful alt text to images
options.rationale: Correct: alt text describes images for people using screen readers.

options.text: Using enough colour contrast between text and background
options.rationale: Correct: good contrast makes text readable for more people.

options.text: Making all text the same colour as the background
options.rationale: Matching colours hides the text and harms readability.

options.text: Removing all headings from the page
options.rationale: Headings help structure and navigation; removing them hurts access.

items.explanation: Correct: alt text describes images for people using screen readers.

items.stem: You want three boxes to share the same colours and spacing. What is the tidiest CSS approach?

options.text: Give them the same class and style that class once
options.rationale: Correct: a shared class lets you style many elements with one rule.

options.text: Copy the same styles onto each box separately
options.rationale: Repeating styles is harder to maintain than a shared class.
Appearance is handled by CSS, using classes.
You do not need separate pages to share styles.

items.explanation: Correct: a shared class lets you style many elements with one rule.
